summary: The milestone-scoped TIMING DATA block fed to this retro reported no experiment commits since activation, so the locked numeric fields are 0/0/0/null. This matches the recurring FALSE-ZERO milestone-timing detector gap flagged across ~74 prior milestones (e.g. .447): the authoritative detector returns zero even when experiments did commit, so per-experiment durations could not be ranked from the authoritative source this milestone. On-disk artifact inspection (documented in the research-log entry) indicates 2026.06.448 actually executed its phase arms; the retro JSON keeps the conductor-locked 0/0/0/null fields per the anti-hallucination guard.
bottlenecks_identified: Recurring FALSE-ZERO milestone-scoped-timing detector gap: the authoritative TIMING DATA block reported 0 commits since activation, so this retro cannot rank slowest experiments or compute a real wall-time from its own data source. The same gap has been documented for ~74 milestones (~.363 through .447); it forces a manual disk-mtime inspection every retro and risks misdiagnosing an active milestone as empty.

Both RTX 3090 GPUs are idle (0% util, 4MB allocated each), but this is CORRECT, not a bottleneck: no monitored-3090 compute-bound task was present in the TIMING DATA, so gpu_idle_on_compute_bound_tasks is null and GPU idle is NOT flagged (per the GPU-idle interpretation rule).
improvements_suggested: Move the shipped milestone-scoped timing detector-wire to the conductor's retro TIMING-DATA prompt-assembly call site so the retro is fed real per-experiment durations instead of a false zero. This is the single recurring operational defect and is the reason the locked fields read 0/0/0/null.

Add a disk-mtime fallback: when the detector returns 0 commits, derive the exp_range and window from results/experiment_*.json mtimes so a detector false-zero degrades to a verifiable artifact-mtime window rather than an apparently-empty retro.

Enforce the Inference-Substrate Declaration Discipline at write time for blocked tasks: a task exiting with honest_verdict=blocked_* MUST NOT declare inference_substrate=live_llm_inference, since it never reached inference -- this prevents benign blocked tasks from tripping the DURATION_TOO_SHORT fabrication gate.
Leave GPU / DualGPURunner untouched: no monitored-3090 compute-bound task ran, so both 3090s idle is correct behaviour, not an inefficiency to fix.
top_3_highest_leverage_actions: Wire real per-experiment timing into the retro TIMING-DATA block (move the detector to the prompt-assembly call site + add a disk-mtime fallback) -- the dominant recurring operational defect across ~74 milestones; it does not reclaim compute wall-clock but eliminates the manual disk inspection every retro requires and prevents misdiagnosing active milestones as empty.
Fix the blocked-task substrate declaration (blocked_* => never live_llm_inference) so benign blocked phase arms stop tripping the fabrication gate.
Do NOT enforce DualGPURunner or any GPU-engagement change: both 3090s idle is correct because no monitored-3090 compute-bound task ran this milestone.
meta_reflection: The honest operational story of this milestone is not 'empty' but 'invisible': the retro's authoritative timing source reported zero while the milestone's phase arms actually ran and committed, the same false-zero detector gap flagged for ~74 milestones. The recurring fix -- real timing into the retro prompt plus a disk-mtime fallback -- is higher-leverage than any per-experiment speedup, because it would stop every future retro from having to reconstruct the execution window by hand and from initially misreading an active milestone as data-free.
